sources.title: Afghanistan Travel Advisory
sources.officialityEvidence: Current State Department advisory issued 2 April 2026, addressed to U.S. citizens and stating the entry rule and current recognition limitation.
sources.supportingExcerpt: An Afghan visa is required to enter and exit Afghanistan. You must apply for a visa before you travel.

sources.title: Entry requirements - Afghanistan travel advice
sources.officialityEvidence: Current FCDO entry page expressly scopes itself to full British-citizen passports from the United Kingdom.
sources.supportingExcerpt: A visa is required to enter Afghanistan. The Afghan embassy in London is closed.

sources.title: Travel advice and advisories for Afghanistan
sources.officialityEvidence: Live Government of Canada destination advice, last updated 29 July 2026, separately identifies a regular Canadian passport and tourist visa requirement.
sources.supportingExcerpt: You must obtain a visa to visit Afghanistan. Tourist visa: Required

sources.title: Viaggiare Sicuri: Afghanistan entry requirements
sources.publisher: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Crisis Unit
sources.officialityEvidence: Live MAECI country PDF gives Italian entry requirements and records current operational uncertainty.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Il visto è obbligatorio. Si sono verificati respingimenti di stranieri muniti di visto.

sources.title: Afghanistan travel advice
sources.officialityEvidence: Live DFA advice stated current at 22 August 2026 and expressly scopes its entry section to Afghanistan travel by Irish citizens.
sources.supportingExcerpt: A visa is required to enter Afghanistan. Afghanistan does not have an Embassy in Ireland and the Afghan Embassy in London is closed.

sources.title: Afghanistan: travel and security advice
sources.officialityEvidence: Current Foreign Office page expressly characterises its entry section as the rules that existed before August 2021 and only believed still applied.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Angaben beziehen sich auf die bis August 2021 bestehende Regeln, die nach Kenntnis des Auswärtigen Amts weiter angewandt werden.

sources.title: Recomendaciones de viaje: Afganistán
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation, Spain
sources.officialityEvidence: Current Spanish Embassy country guidance identifies visa liability but no Afghan authority that presently issues an ordinary Spanish visitor visa.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Para entrar en Afganistán se requiere visado.

sources.title: Recomendaciones de viaje: Corea del Norte
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation, Spain
sources.jurisdiction: Spain / Democratic People's Republic of Korea
sources.officialityEvidence: Current Spanish MFA guidance, valid 24 August 2026, identifies tourist/business visa liability and the only contemplated China/Russia routes, but no issuer or application channel.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Se necesita visado, ya sea por turismo o negocios.

conflicts.officialStatus: unresolved: advance visa liability without a verified operational issuer
conflicts.explanation: The current U.S. advisory states that a visa is required before travel but warns that Republic-era mission visas may be refused unless issued by an authority aligned with the de facto government. No cited current Afghan issuer is shown as available to ordinary U.S. tourist-passport applicants, so the advance-visa label is not operationally established.

unresolved.reason: The current U.S. advisory establishes visa liability before travel but no current Afghan issuer available to ordinary U.S. tourist-passport applicants. Republic-era mission visas may be refused, so an operational advance route is not established.
Germany presents only pre-August-2021 rules it believes may still apply; its Republic-era mission referral does not prove a current accepted issuer or actual pre-travel issuance.
FCDO confirms a visa requirement for a full British-citizen passport but says the Afghan Embassy in London is closed and identifies no alternative operational issuer or timing.
MAECI confirms visa liability but reports refusals even for visa holders and identifies no current ordinary-visitor issuing authority or pre-travel route.
No current Polish authority source and no accessible current Afghan mission source together establish an ordinary Polish-passport visitor liability and operational pre-travel issuing route.
Spain confirms visa liability, but the current advisory identifies no presently accepted Afghan issuer, application point, or actual ordinary-visitor issuance before travel.

Canada identifies a required tourist visa for a regular Canadian passport but does not identify a current issuer or establish that a visa can actually be obtained before travel amid severe border restrictions.
Ireland confirms visa liability, but says there is no Afghan Embassy in Ireland and the London Embassy is closed; no alternate accepted issuing channel or timing is established.
No current Polish government or DPRK authority source establishes an operational ordinary Polish tourist pre-travel visa issuer. Historical Warsaw-embassy material is not current-force proof.
Spain's current MFA advice establishes tourist/business visa liability and China/Russia route constraints, but no current DPRK issuer, application channel, approval, or issuance timing.
No current Irish government or DPRK authority source directly establishes an ordinary Irish-passport short-visitor visa issuer or operational advance-issuance route.
